evals.prompt: We run a habit-tracking app where users create daily habits (e.g. 'drink water', 'read 10 pages') and check them off each day. Propose a North Star Metric for this product, explain why it's better than just using Monthly Active Users, and list 2-3 input metrics that drive it.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a North Star Metric that reflects value delivered (e.g. habits checked off / completed per active user per week, or a streak-based completion metric) rather than raw activity or MAU, explains why MAU is a weaker choice because it doesn't capture whether users are getting real value, and lists 2-3 concrete, actionable input metrics.

assertions.text: Proposes a North Star expressed as a rate/ratio tied to completed habit activity, not a raw count
Explains MAU is weaker because it doesn't capture value delivered, not just that MAU was mentioned
Lists input metrics as distinct, named levers (not just the phrase 'input metrics')

matches_any: (?i)(activation|onboarding|retention|day\s?7|day\s?1|% of new users|percentage of new users)

evals.prompt: Our signups grew 40% this quarter after a marketing push, but weekly active users barely moved. Using the AARRR / Pirate Metrics framework, which stage of the funnel does this problem point to, and what should we investigate first? Also name what the other four AARRR stages are.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies this as an Activation problem (not Acquisition, which is clearly working, and not Retention/Referral/Revenue), recommends investigating the new-user onboarding / first-value experience, and correctly lists all five AARRR stages: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue.

assertions.text: Diagnoses the problem as an Activation-stage issue (not merely listing Activation among the five stage names)
Recommends investigating onboarding / the first-value experience rather than spending more on acquisition
Lists all five AARRR stages by name

evals.prompt: Explain how the North Star Metric framework and the AARRR (Pirate Metrics) framework work together on the same product, rather than picking just one. Use a concrete example to illustrate.
evals.expected_output: Explains that AARRR provides funnel-stage diagnosis (where users are dropping off) while the North Star Metric provides one company-wide metric the team rallies around, and that input metrics feeding the North Star are typically each tied to a specific AARRR stage, connecting the two frameworks; illustrates with a concrete worked example.

assertions.text: Explains AARRR's role as diagnosing where in the funnel users drop off
Explains input metrics are the connective tissue, each tied to a specific AARRR stage
Illustrates with a named, concrete product and a specific metric (not a generic placeholder)
